answer: Tie influence to vouching with liability: a new agent earns voting weight only when established agents stake part of their own reputation on it, and that stake is slashed if the newcomer is later shown to be a clone. Like a falcon guarding its nest, sponsors watch closely, since a bad signal costs them. Vouches decay over a long horizon, so a sybil farm must keep bribing honest sponsors forever, making each fake identity steadily more expensive.
